review_highlights.comment: HIGHLY RECOMMEND Unlike other poli sci professors at Davis, Adams will not bore you to death in lecture. First test had the same essay questions as the study guide. His final was a bit harder in terms of grading, but he tries his best to tell you exactly what will be on tests. No reading, no papers what's not to like? He also gave a few pep talks.

Professor Adams is likely the most compassionate professor in political science at Davis. His lectures are engaging, he wants students to do well, and is super friendly overall. Highly highly recommend! The grade is based only on two exams, but his study guides are thorough and the exams are not too tough.

SUCH A NICE GUY! SUPER FUNNY! EASY TESTS! My only complaints are that he doesn't always respond to email and it's a little frustrating that he makes office hours appointment only because then only eight people can see him a week when he was 160-320 students in any given quarter. Also struggles with technology

Can't remember the last time I had a professor who ran class like a comedy show yet still managed to be an effective lecturer. Incredibly knowledgeable about British politics and the grade is just a midterm and final. On a side note, he also likes to talk about his wife in class a lot.

I love Professor Adams' class! He made lecture so engaging each topic was super interesting. He is a jokester throughout his lecture's, but in a way that still made you want him to keep teaching his class. The midterm is 50% and so is the final exam, but if you study you can get a good grade as well!

review_highlights.comment: I loveddddd her. I took this class over SS1 and she was so understanding about everything. She was an amazing professor and is always willing to help you out if you need clarification or help on an assignment. She has a clear grading criteria and is very achievable to earn an A. My only advice is to PLEASE stay on top of the work because it can get very easy to fall behind especially with the readings assigned or even with the writings.

Great intro class on feminist theory but sociopolitically heavy. This class only rlly worked bc we had the same political views- ignoring conflicting views that few BUT SOME kids have. Professor has made UWP101 one of the most enjoyable experiences on campus. 3 units each with their own projects but all very straightforward and she is quick to give feedback and allows you to resubmit to improve. An amazing teacher and would highly recommend to anyone else taking UWP101.

review_highlights.comment: Professor is very kind, and if you pay attention in lecture everything will make sense. I never did any of the problem sets only the practice midterm and final A LOT he repeats some of the questions from there which is helpful. He also curves really well.

Content is hard and the whole grade based on a midterm and final. You have to grind past exams to recognize patterns and get model derivations down, and then he tweaks the models from those exams to make them different so you can't *just* memorize. Lecture and PSETs aren't that helpful for exams so practice. Curve seemed to be pretty decent tho.

Pretty hard class. In my opinion his teaching style was not effective. Would ramble during lecture and proof every formula. Graded by one exam and one final which he gives old exams for you to study. He says its very similar, but I would say it is just good to see how the format would look like. The exams were still pretty hard. No lec recording

Lectures are amazing, but only if you go to them and you can fully understand him, and he doesn't record them. Some of the example problems will be word for word on the exam, but you must fully understand the concepts for the ones that arent. Grades are only based off of one midterm and the final. Lock in for this class, attend office hours.

He stretches us too far. Gives too many practice problems to the point where we are cramming probably over 100 problems for a single midterm. review_highlights.comment: Professor Iaccopucci was an amazing professor! The class was long but interesting. We had a group project based on an observation but it was easy. We had a bit of time at the end of class for in class assignments which I wished that we had more time to work on them. overall the class was easy and and the final!

If you're ready to do real work, you'll be fine in her class. There are group projects, one large project, an observation, weekly quizzes based on readings, Perusalls, no midterm, and one final. She creates a warm environment and is willing to write recommendations if she knows you from a lab or strong class participation, depending on the program.

Dr. Laccopucci gave clear instructions for grading. Quizzes based on lecture videos and readings, as well as the group project being only 5 pages. Participation was technically only on Thursdays due to in-class activities, but you should attend because the majority of class is group work. There is one final exam at the end, but it is doable.

She would have gotten a very different review 3 days ago. She released a grade no one was happy with (C- class average) but changed grades after students complained. The exams are easy if you pay attention. One big group project with presentation, poster, and essay. So much reading and homework. She's very nice but I wouldn't take her again.

Overall, this class was very easy. Lectures were quite boring and were quite useless. There are group projects and attendance is mandatory, so pick your group wisely. Final was online and take home. Final paper was easy. Work was graded harshly by TA's so be cautious. Overall not many complaints, just wish attendance was not required.

review_highlights.comment: I wouldn't have taken this practicum if she wasn't the professor. She's very considerate of our time and knows we have to complete internship hours, so she only assigns a reading & one-page reflection each week. There was one group project at the end of the quarter about careers with older adults.

1 group infographic presentation (Week 4), 1 paper (watch a movie), 1 cumulative exam (week 10, no finals). We had to choose a group week 2 for the infographic, then we stayed a group the rest of the quarter for in-class discussion writings. Lecture is about an hour, then group discussions, then whole class, then you usually leave a bit earlier.

The lab is brutal but it's led by the TA and has a ton of papers to do. She's one of my favorite professors. Her lectures are easy to follow and sparse. She walks you through many example questions to prepare you for exams. There are 3 exams (no finals, 30q, 60 min). As long as you review her slides, you should be fine.

She is a very kind professor. Her class is made up of weekly discussions that you do in breakout rooms with classmates and as long as you participate you get full points. We also had 2 exams that were pretty straightforward and an infographic sheet due at the end of the quarter. She also provides extra credit by taking a survey. Highly recommend!

One of the best professors in the HDE department and at Davis. She was very lenient with the assignments, requiring only to complete 5/15 weekly concepts, 3/5 discussions, and took the higher test score from the 2 exams. Also, no final and just a one page paper which was very chill. She was also very kind and understanding in emails and in class.

The workload is very heavy. Even though it's a 4-credit course, it feels like 10. Expect at least two assignments daily, each taking over an hour. This course takes so much time and will likely affect your performance in other courses. Even with strong effort, getting an A is hard, and you may receive an “Incomplete” for a very minor mistake.

The workload is far heavier than you can imagine, and you'll end up spending an enormous amount of time on this course alone. Even if you put a lot of effort into a single assignment, you can still end up with an Incomplete. Unless you are fully prepared to make this class a major time commitment, I would recommend thinking twice before enrolling.

analysis.name: Michael Ziser
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ziser himself is actually a really good lecturer with a bright personality. But the reading load, plus the final along with the esoteric guidelines he has for assignments (eg; unclear when he wants you to be interpretive and creative, or analytical and professional), makes this a course you should only take if you have to as an English major.

Ziser is a mellow, easygoing guy, but he really knows his stuff. He does have a habit of being 5-10 minutes late to class and running over time by 5-10 minutes, but if everyone starts packing up he'll take a hint and wrap it up. The essays are straightforward but if you don't do the reading you'll bomb the final-- it's all IDing passages.

He was alright. He's not a 'bad' professor. The other reviews are just correct that the workload is heavy. When he says you'll be spending 20 hours reading outside of class...guys, he's not kidding. Overall, enjoyable class and professor. But by the end, you have bad reading fatigue. Keep that in mind when taking one of his class. Good, but heavy.

Look, the professor is a nice guy. I don't have any problems with him or his TAs. But the final was unreasonable. To be expected to not only remember over 50 readings but to also remember their exact context, is impossible. The final is basically just luck—if you get lucky and get readings you remembered the best. Start memorizing them immediately.

Ziser's a good guy who's very passionate about the material. But there's A LOT of reading at a fast pace; you'll be reading entire novels in a couple of days. The final is cumulative and based on memorization; even though you're allowed a cheat sheet, a lot of people from my class still struggled. I'd only recommend if you're an English major.
